To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

perceived usefulness, perceived ease of usabili-ty and information quality have positive effects on continuance intention, whereas perceived ease of use has an indirect effect on continuance intention.

(1) the perceived performance construct is decomposed into two dimensions: perceived quality and perceived usefulness; (2) the decomposed technology acceptance (DTAM) model provides a better explanation of the determinants of continuance intention than the TAM model; (3) perceived quality and confirmation have significant positive impacts on satisfaction; (4) perceived ease of use has a significant negative effect on satisfaction, and (5) cognitive absorption is not an antecedent of satisfaction.

perceived performance, perceived ease of usability, perceived ease of ease of use, perceived ease of usefulness, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of ease all contribute to the intention to use e-learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors that influence the continuance intention to use e-learning services.
understanding how e-learning services are adopted and sustained by the users in the context of higher education in China.
the factors that influence the continuance intention of e-learning service users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model has a good fit with the empirical data and is able to explain a large portion of the variation in the continuance intention to use e-learning services.

the results of this study suggest that users' continuance intention is jointly determined by satisfaction, perceived usefulness, information, service quality, confirmation, system quality, and cognitive absorption.

the results of this study have demonstrated that perceived performance (i.e. perceived quality and perceived ease of use) and confirmation (i.e. confirmation and cognitive absorption) are the key determinants of user satisfaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model is an effective tool for understanding users' continuance intention in e-learning services, which can be used to improve e-learning systems.
the Technology Acceptance model (TAM) is not sufficient in explaining the intention to continue using e-learning systems.

we have proposed a model that explains the determinants of continuance intention in an e-learning service and that the proposed model is a valid and reliable model for the context of an online learning environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decomposed technology acceptance models are more effective than the original technology acceptance model in explaining users’ continuance intentions.
